title: Instrument Trace event
description: One action taken on an instrument, by anyone (agent, GUI, script, job), with enough context to rebuild the run and to learn rewards from it. Written as one JSON object per line. Fields added in 1.1.0 (seq, written, writer, run, simulated, clock) are optional, so lines written before them still validate; asyncroscopy.trace.stream reads both.

ts.description: Wall-clock Unix time when the action started.

source.description: Kind of writer: mcp, job, approvals, script; analysis for pyTEMlib's trace. Any other name is allowed so new writers need no schema change.

writer.description: Who wrote the line: a Tango device name (asyncroscopy/mapper/default), mcp:<server name>:<role>, or <source>@<host>:<pid>.

seq.description: The line's number in its file: rises by one per line, whichever process appended it (a lock shared by every writer of the file), and keeps rising across a rotation of the file.

written.description: Unix time the line was appended, never earlier than the line before it in the same file. Readers merge files by it.

action.description: Tool or command name, e.g. Mapper_start or move_stage.

arguments.description: The call's arguments as given. Recorded in full (results are cut to a preview): the trace is not a place for secrets.

result.description: Short result preview; large data are referenced by result_key.

run.description: The agent run (the X-Asyncroscopy-Run header) the action belongs to; absent when no run is known (a GUI or script call).

approved_by.description: 'auto' when the mode let it through, the operator's name when approved, null if not gated.

run_id.description: A job's reservation id (not the agent run: see run).

simulated.description: True when the stack drives a simulator (run_servers' top-level simulated:), false on hardware; absent when the writer cannot tell.

dry_run.description: Job events: true on every event of a dry-run job, false on a real one (lines before 1.1.0 left it out on a real one).

performed.description: Dry run only: true for the calls that really ran (blank_beam), false for those only recorded.

device.description: Dry run only: the device a recorded call was addressed to.

check.description: Dry run only: the job's check of a recorded call, e.g. a move_stage against the plan box.

clock_s.description: The instrument's clock (simulated seconds on a twin, Unix time on hardware): for a job step, when the step finished; otherwise when the event was written. See clock.

clock.description: Where clock_s came from: the instrument's clock_s attribute, or this computer's time when the writer has no instrument clock or could not read it.
